articleTitle: A Parallel Read-Write Circuit Design for Driving Memristor Crossbar Array
abstract: Memristor crossbar array is considered as a promising circuit module for accelerating neural networks. Because the memristor is tunable and multi-state, it is important to design applicable Read-Write (RW) circuit for driving memristor crossbar array. In this paper, a novel RW circuit based on analog circuits is proposed for tuning memristors in high-dimensional array parallelly, which is scalable and low-overhead. The standalone RW circuit schematic is presented for reading/writing single memristor and verified in circuit simulation. Then, we extend and apply this circuit into a two-dimensional memristor crossbar array. The performance of memristor crossbar array controlled by designed RW circuits is verified via the simulations under various machine learning datasets. The comparison with related works is presented, which demonstrates the advantages of the proposed RW circuit regarding overhead and anti-error.

articleTitle: Aggregative Games on a Strongly Connected Digraphs
abstract: This paper considers the distributed Nash equilibrium seeking strategy for aggregative games. We consider the game to have no central-node and the aggregated information is not directly available to the players. Therefore, we consider a average consensus protocol is adopted to estimate the aggregate information. By introducing a surplus variable, the changing states of each player’s integral terms are recorded in real-time. Combining the average consensus protocol with gradient descent method, we establish a distributed strategy for seeking Nash equilibrium in aggregative games under strongly connected nonequilibrium directed topologies and prove the algorithm’s convergence. Finally, a numerical example is presented to validate the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Reachable Set Bounding for Delay Second-Order Memristive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper focuses on the reachable set bounding problem of delayed second-order memristive neural networks (DSMNNs). By introducing the inertial term into memristive neural networks (MNNs), MNNs are modeled as second-order differential equations with discontinuous right-hand sides. By using nonsmooth analysis, Lyapunov stability theory and inequality techniques, a feedback controller is constructed to guarantee all the states of DSMNNs are bounding in a set. Here, the reduced-order analysis method is employed. The new reachable set estimation conditions proposed are represented as algebraic criteria, which are tested easily. At last, numerical simulation is provided to show the validity of the derived results.

articleTitle: Pinning Synchronization of Fractional-Order Two-Layer Networks: From Inter-Layer Synchronization to Cluster Synchronization
abstract: This article is dedicated to the cluster synchronization problem of fractional-order two-layer networks (FOTLNs) in two steps. The first step is to implement the inter-layer synchronization of FOTLNs by designing a partial directed inter-layer communication mode and a novel feedback controller imposed on the first layer network. Especially, a new method of treating a layer network as a whole is used, which provides an important idea for the analysis of inter-layer synchronization of the FOTLNs. On the basis of the first step, by designing pinning control strategy employed on the second layer network, the cluster synchronization of the FOTLNs is solved, subsequently. Note that the cluster synchronization of the FOTLNs are guaranteed only when the designed two controllers are activated simultaneously, which can be extended to the investigation of the cluster synchronization of networks with the single layer, the multi-layers or the integer order. Two illustrative examples are provided lastly to confirm the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Multiple Unmanned Surface Vehicle Coverage Control in Dynamic Environments
abstract: This paper investigates the area coverage problem for multiple Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) in dynamic environments. Multiple USVs are employed to execute the coverage task using the Voronoi Partition method for task allocation. Parameter adaptive laws are employed to estimate the parameters of the sensing function and the Voronoi cell centroids for updating the target positions in dynamic environments. Additionally, considering the influence of water surface disturbances, a nonholonomic underactuated model analysis is conducted for the USV under non-full constraints, resulting in a motion strategy for USVs. This enables the multiple USVs to effectively cover the task area. Finally, simulation results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the coverage scheme designed in this paper and the ability of USVs to effectively cover dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Output Synchronization of T-S Fuzzy Complex Networks with Mismatched Parameters
abstract: This article is devoted to the analysis of fixed-time (FXT) output synchronization for a kind of complex networks (CNs) involving T-S fuzzy logic and mismatched parameters. To begin with, a class of discontinuous fuzzy control protocol is proposed based on fuzzy theory, which is crucial for handing the fuzziness of the CNs and ensuring FXT output synchronization. Subsequently, by employing inequality technique and the improved FXT stability theorem, several effective criteria are established to realize FXT output synchronization. Additionally, the constraint on the output matrix with diagonal and positive definite form is removed. To conclude, an illustrative example is given to confirm the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Three-Dimensional Cooperative Guidance Law for Moving Target with Line-of-Sight Angle Constraint
abstract: A new kind of finite-time three-dimensional cooperative guidance laws with Line-of-sight (LOS) that guarantees the intercept of moving targets is proposed in this paper. Firstly, through careful and rigorous analysis of the cooperative guidance systems, a finite-time observer is designed to observer states of the moving target. Then, a cooperative guidance law via the finite-time control theory is proposed to intercept the target under the user-defined LOS angle constraint. Finally, simulation studies are provided to illustrate the advantages of the proposed guidance law.

articleTitle: On Optimization of Multi-machine PSS Parameters Tuning Based on SCSO Algorithm
abstract: This paper addresses the optimization of power system stabilizer parameters for improving the stability of multi-machine power system. A relatively new algorithm, namely sand cat swarm optimization, is utilized to optimize some control parameters of power system stabilizer. Compared with some relative methods, the power system stabilizer based on the proposed sand cat swarm optimization algorithm can realize the stability more quickly. Finally, the validity of obtained methods are substantiated by a IEEE 4-machine 2-zone system.

articleTitle: Brain Inspired Episodic Memory Deep Q-Networks for Sparse Reward
abstract: Although deep reinforcement learning has achieved great success in recent years, it still suffers from slow convergence, low sample efficiency, and large computational resources due to the existence of reward sparsity in many decision problems. Therefore, exploring more effective algorithms that can cope with sparse rewards is of great importance. Episodic memory reinforcement learning has received a lot of attention for its ability to collect past dominant strategies, which can serve as successful experiences to efficiently guide agents in sparse reward environments. In this paper, the episodic memory deep Q-networks, which incorporates the fast convergence property of episodic memory into neural networks, is employed to solve decision making problem with sparse rewards. Atari games are the test beds. Experiments show that the episodic memory deep Q-networks outperforms the deep Q-networks and the prioritized experience replay, which demonstrates the sample efficiency and the effectiveness of episodic memory deep Q-networks for the sparse reward problem.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Garbage Classification System Based on Deep Learning
abstract: This paper aims to discuss the design and development of garbage classification system using deep learning, which can effectively and accurately classify garbage. The method based on transfer learning is used, because the pre-training model can extract the basic features of the image, which slows down the occurrence of over fitting to a certain extent. And it is transferred to the garbage image dataset for fine tuning training to improve the recognition accuracy. Additionally, a method combining threshold segmentation and edge detection has been adopted. The system uses MobileNetv2 as the core to build a lightweight feature extraction network, and optimize and improve its model, so as to finally achieve high-precision classification effect.

articleTitle: A General Method for Drawing Fractal Graphs Using Dynamical System
abstract: At present, fractal graphs are mainly drawn by iterative function system. This paper presents a general method of drawing fractal graphs by dynamic system. As long as the dynamic system satisfying the drawing conditions is given, the fractal graph corresponding to it can be drawn by the general method designed in this paper. Firstly, this paper introduces the principle that many points in the plot area will escape under the action of dynamic system. Then, the fractal graph drawing algorithm with dynamic system is designed. Finally, the algorithm is tested. The key technique of this method is to establish the condition of function selection execution in a dynamic system. The test results show that this method can realize partial fractal graph drawing. The design of this method provides a general method that can be used to draw fractal graph by dynamic system, and it is a supplement and perfection to fractal graph method.

articleTitle: Memristor-Based Analog Multiplier
abstract: Memristors, as a novel non-volatile circuit component, hold significant promise in electronic circuit applications. This article presents a novel memristor-based multiplier design, consisting of three key stages: an absolute value circuit, a multiplication circuit, and a sign circuit. The multiplier is capable of performing multiplication operations within the range of 1V to 10V, and it can achieve multiplication even when both input values are set to zero through deliberate circuit design, thereby eliminating the need for analog-to-digital signal conversion. This innovation reduces circuit complexity and energy consumption, enhancing overall circuit efficiency.

articleTitle: A Multi-Scale CNN-ViT Network with Squeeze-and-Excitation Block for ECG Signal Classification
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a widely utilized diagnostic tool for detecting different cardiac irregularities, including atrial fibrillation, bradycardia, and other anomalies in the heart’s electrical activity. Menwhile, CNN-ViT networks have recently demonstrated strong performance in various computer vision tasks. In this paper, we propose a CNN-ViT network specifically designed for the ECG classification task. Our method combines the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformer (ViT) networks. Convolutional block is employed to capture local ECG features, while the ViT block extracts global features. By integrating CNN and ViT, our network benefits from leveraging both local and global information for the ECG classification task. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our network compared to previous baseline approachs on the CPSC dataset and the Chapman dataset in terms of performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Triggered Distributed Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems with External Disturbances
abstract: This paper is devoted to the distributed optimization issue for multi-agent systems (MASs) with external interferences. Firstly, a distributed protocol with dynamic event-triggered (DET) communication is proposed to avert continuous communication among intelligent agents, here an auxiliary variable is introduced for each individual to adjust dynamically its threshold. Then, it is proved that under the DET mechanism, the lower bound of the inter-event time between consecutive triggering moments is positive and the Zeno phenomenon is naturally eliminated. Moreover, the exponential convergence of the MASs is ensured and the external disturbance is rejected via utilizing the internal model (IM) principle. The proposed protocol is illustrated lastly by providing a specific example.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Stabilization of Inertial Competitive Neural Networks With Proportional Delays
abstract: This paper mainly focuses on the problems of finite-time (F-T) stabilization of inertial competitive neural networks (ICNNs) with proportional delays. Firstly, as opposed to converting the second-order systems into the first-order systems through the approach of reduced order, this study directly constructs the Lyapunov function on the original ICNNs, which can yield more accurate results. Then, the criteria for F-T stabilization of ICNNs with two different types of controllers are presented based on the theory of F-T stability.

articleTitle: Opinion Evolution in the FJ Model with Oblivious Individuals in Cooperation-Competition Networks
abstract: This article investigates the evolution of individual opinions with oblivious individuals in a cooperation-competition network. By building an individual opinion evolution model with oblivious individuals under cooperation-competition networks, and giving a proof on the convergence of the opinions of individuals in structural unbalance and structural balance with respect to the influence weight matrices $w_{22}$ among oblivious individuals, the individual opinion evolution characteristics of $w_{22}$ in different states are obtained, and finally, corresponding simulations are given to verify the authenticity and correctness of the conclusions.

articleTitle: Robust ψ-Type Stability of Memristor-Based Neural Networks with Unbounded Time-Varying Delay Under Input Perturbation
abstract: Investigating the robustness of memristor-based neural networks (MNNs) under disturbances is crucial since robustness improves the practical effectiveness of neural networks. This article investigates the robustness and the multiple $\psi$-type stability for MNNs with unbounded time-varying delay under input perturbation. New criteria for boundedness and $\psi$-type stability of MNNs under input perturbation which satisfies some conditions are provided through pure analysis methods.

articleTitle: Specific-Time Unknown Input Observer for Lur’e System
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of specific-time state estimation for Lur’e systems with unknown inputs. By analyzing nonlinear Lur’e systems, sufficient conditions for the design of unknown input observers are provided. Then, a specific-time observer is designed, with convergence analysis illustrated. The main advantage of the designed observer can realize accurate estimation of Lur’e system in specific time. Finally, a simulation example of the third-order Chua’s circuit is conducted to verify the validity of the proposed specific-time unknown input observer.

articleTitle: Research on Chinese Speech Synthesis Based on Multiple Attention Fusion Scoring Mechanism
abstract: Currently, fully end-to-end speech synthesis techniques based on conditional variational autoencoders (CVAEs) are widely popular. However, text-to-speech(TTS) models, led by variational inference with adversarial learning for end-to-end Text-to-Speech (VITS), tend to exhibit significant prosodic issues when synthesizing Chinese speech, thereby requiring further improvements in synthesis quality compared to other languages. Therefore, considering the linguistic and prosodic characteristics of Chinese, this study applies special phonetic mapping during data preprocessing and integrates three different attention mechanisms into the VITS model for fully end-to-end speech synthesis. This approach aims to achieve highly natural Chinese speech synthesis. The proposed model is validated through theoretical analysis and experiments. Additionally, a public Chinese speech dataset from Baker is utilized for training, and the synthesized speech quality is evaluated subjectively and objectively. The subjective evaluation involves a group of participants assessing the naturalness and fluency of the synthesized speech, while the objective evaluation measures the Euclidean distance between the mel cepstral coefficients of the synthesized and real speech. The experimental results show that the improved model can synthesize more real and natural Chinese speech, which has certain guiding significance.

articleTitle: A Novel Method of Fixed-time Synchronization of Neural Networks
abstract: This paper has addressed the fixed-time synchronization of neural networks. Aiming to realize fixed-time synchronization of driven-response system, two different structures of controllers are established based on finite-time theorem. Different from the existing methods, the powers of controllers’ fractional term can vary with the value of states, which lead controller to be simpler and can be tolerant to disturbances or uncertainties. Moreover, corresponding conditions to select controllers’ parameters are given out. Finally, a numerical example with simulations is employed to validate the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: On Predefined-time Synchronization of Complex-valued Neural Networks With Inertial Terms
abstract: This paper investigates the predefined-time synchronization of a specific type of inertial complex-valued neural networks (ICVNNs). By employing the reduced-order transformations and the methods for dividing the real part from the imaginary part, the ICVNNs are converted into first-order real-valued differential equations. Additionally, the analysis of predefined-time synchronization is presented on the basis of the Lyapunov function. Finally, simulation examples are included to elaborate the rationality and applicability of the obtained results.

articleTitle: Improved Two-Step Finite-Time Stabilization Control for Time-Delay Systems
abstract: In this article, an improved two-step control method is developed to achieve the finite-time stabilization for the general nonlinear systems with bounded time-varying delay. In the first step, the system attenuates from V($t_{0}$) to qV($t_{0}$) by the Halanay inequality, where $0\lt q \leq 1$ is a free parameter. In the second step, by using existing finite-time stability theorem, the system decays from qV($t_{0}$) to 0. Based on the above ideas, a novel finite-time stability theorem for the controlled time-delay systems is rendered. And, the convergence rate and the settling time of the finite-time stability of the system are also estimated. Furthermore, the value of q with the shortest settling time for the system is given. The attained result is applied to the finite-time stabilization of a kind of nonlinear systems by designing a switching controller. Finally, the validity of the analytical results attained in this article are shown by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Classification of Oil Paintings Based on Improved Vision Transformer
abstract: As the trend of digitizing art paintings grows, oil paintings categorizing becomes more and more important. Artworks exhibit diverse styles, making it a challenge to simultaneously capture both their global and intricate features. Addressing this issue, this paper introduces a Bilinear vision transformer Neural Network (BViTNN) that leverages the vision transformer for extracting fine-grained features and employs Convolution Neural Network(CNN) for extracting low-level semantic features. The utilization of DropKey enhances the generalization capacity and global feature capture of the vision transformer. The proposed network demonstrates an outstanding performance on a self-created dataset comprising 7227 images for the classification of 49 artists, achieving an impressive classification accuracy of 86%. Furthermore, this study explores data augmentation techniques on the custom dataset, revealing that the use of random erasing and Gaussian blurring enhances the training accuracy of the network.

articleTitle: Discriminating Stability of Hybrid Stochastic Delay Neural Networks: A Novel Approach
abstract: This article presents a new approach for studying the mean square exponential stability of nonlinear stochastic delay neural networks with Markov chains. Explicit identities are derived to characterize the stability properties of these systems. Both delay-independent and delay-dependent stability theorems are provided based on these identities. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through an illustrative example.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Distributed Output Optimization for Linear Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: The article is devoted to fixed-time (FXT) output optimization for multi-agent systems (MASs) by proposing distributed piecewise protocols. Firstly, the FXT tracking of the agent states is ensured by introducing an auxiliary variable for each agent. Then, under the out information of agents and the strong convexity of cost functions, a distributed piecewise algorithm is developed, which indicates that the FXT distributed output optimization is solved by first realizing local optimization for each agent and then achieving global output optimization. In addition, a more relaxed condition for FXT distributed optimization is derived and a more precise estimate for the optimization time is obtained. Finally, the proposed optimization algorithm is further illustrated via numerical results.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Synchronization of Flux-Controlled Complex-Valued Memristive Neural Networks
abstract: In this paper, by using the flux-controlled memristor model, the finite-time synchronization problem of delayed complex-valued memristive neural networks (MCNNs) is studied. Firstly, according to the proposed memristor model, we model the MCNNs as continuous systems on voltage-flux-time $(\wp, \varpi, t)$ domain. Then, we design a class of approaches to realize state synchronization between the drive and response systems, and the corresponding synchronization conditions are achieved. Finally, the effectiveness of results is illustrated with the simulations.

articleTitle: Meta-Transfer Learning with Attention for Marine Aquaculture Information Extraction
abstract: Floating raft aquaculture is a crucial marine aquaculture method, the difference of floating raft aquaculture in different regions in remote sensing images brings challenges to marine aquaculture monitoring by deep learning information extraction. Meta-transfer learning with attention (MTLA) approach is proposed in this paper. Before the meta-training phase, a data enhancement module is included in the network framework to address the problem of few-task scenarios in meta-learning. Transfer attention block designed specifically for extracting information from SAR images by combining the strengths of transfer learning and attention mechanisms to enhance the capability of feature extraction. Actual GF-3 SAR images from different areas are utilized to verify the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Robust Safety-Critical Control of Nonlinear Systems with External Disturbances
abstract: This paper proposes a robust safety-critical control design approach for nonlinear systems subjected to external disturbances. The external disturbances are modeled by a linear exogenous system, representing a class of partially known harmonic disturbances. To address such disturbances, a corresponding nonlinear disturbance observer is designed for estimation. By utilizing the estimated disturbance from the disturbance observer, novel Control Barrier Function (CBF) constraints and Control Lyapunov Function (CLF) constraints are formulated. Subsequently, a safety-critical controller based on Nonlinear Disturbance Observer-Control Lyapunov Function-Control Barrier Function-Quadratic Programming (NDOB-CLF-CBF-QP) is designed to suppress the disturbances, ensuring the safety and stability of the nonlinear system. Finally, a numerical simulation is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method through comparisons with existing approaches.

articleTitle: Text Sentiment and Semantic Networks Analysis for MOOC Review Texts
abstract: This paper uses web crawler technology to retrieve the review data of six high-quality courses in MOOC English. Review texts are pre-processed and sentiment analysis is performed by using ROSTCM6. After that, TF-IDF is used to calculate the vector matrix, and the number of clusters is determined by the “elbow method”. Finally, K-means is used to cluster negative sentiment comments. Each category is visualized and analyzed for feature extraction. Based on sentiment analysis, three suggestions for MOOC English courses are finally put forward.

articleTitle: Dynamic Characteristic Analysis of FN-HR Neural Network Based on Synapse Coupling of Bistable Memristor
abstract: A hyperbolic bistable memristor model with asymmetric hysteresis loops in different initial states is designed. A memristor synaptic coupled FN-HR neural network is constructed by using the Fitzhugh-Nagumo model and the Hindmarsh-Rose model. The complex dynamic characteristics of the memristor coupling neuron is verified by analyzing the Lyapunov exponent diagram and bifurcation diagram and the equivalent circuit of coupled neural network is designed to prove the accuracy of the numerical analysis.

articleTitle: Preassigned-Time Synchronization of Memristive Chaotic Circuit via Intermittent Control
abstract: In this paper, the preassigned-time synchronization (PTS) problem for a fifth-order memristive chaotic circuit (MCC) is investigated by designing a time-dependent intermittent controller. First, the dynamic characteristics of the MCC, especially the existence and occurrence of chaos, are investigated by simulation experiments. Besides, the stability of the equilibrium points is discussed by using Routh-Hurwitz criterion. Then, a time-dependent intermittent controller is designed and the PTS of MCC is realized via the presented controller. Finally, the effectiveness of theoretical results is verified by means of numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Associative Memory Design Based on Region Attracivity Neural Networks and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel associative memory design method based on neural networks which are region attractivity. For the given memory patterns, we can take any value for networks connection weights and then compute network external inputs based on reinforcement learning algoritms. One numerical experiment is given for validify our method.

articleTitle: Tibetan Few-Shot Learning Model Based on Matching Networks
abstract: This paper highlights the low-resource Tibetan few-shot learning model and establishes accuracy benchmarks utilizing Matching Networks (MN). Addressing the issues of low quality and limited usability in the existing Tibetan-Chinese parallel corpus, this paper constructs a small-scale and high-quality Tibetan-Chinese parallel corpus containing 110,000 sentence pairs using data filtering, deduplication, deletion of blank lines, and special symbol processing. Based on full context embeddings, Softmax-based attention mechanisms, and similarity metrics, the Tibetan few-shot learning model based on MN is proposed to help the model learn logical Tibetan knowledge rapidly from few-shot data. Different distance metrics on Cosine, Euclidean, Poincare, and Minkowski distances are used to test the accuracy of the Tibetan k-shot learning model, which provides a unified and reliable benchmark for the Tibetan few-shot learning tasks. This research provides substantial assistance in solving the issues of machine learning performing poorly in low-resource settings. The experiment results demonstrate that the accuracy of all metrics is improved with the number of shots increased, and Euclidean distance performs well in 5-way 1-shot learning, cosine performs well in 5-way 2-shot learning, and Minkowski distance $(\mathrm{p}=3)$ shows excellent accuracy in 5-way 3-shot learning. Notably, we used our own Tibetan data set and succeeded in enhancing accuracy by a noteworthy 1.6% in a 5-way 3-shot setup.

articleTitle: Anti-Synchronization in Fixed/Prescribed-Time for BAM Memristive Neural Networks with Time-Varying Delays
abstract: This paper is concerned with the fixed-time anti-synchronization (FTAS) and prescribed-time anti-synchronization (PTAS) for bidirectional associative memory memristive neural networks (BAMMNNs) with time-varying delays. By designing unified state-feedback controllers, in light of the Lyapunov function and some inequality techniques, several conditions for the FTAS are obtained for the drive-response systems. Besides, the conditions of PTAS are also explored by adjusting the controllers, and the corresponding settling time (ST) is estimated as well, which can be prescribed according to actual needs and is irrelevant with any initial value and any parameter. Finally, a numerical simulation is given to verify the correctness of the results.

articleTitle: Fixed/preassigned-time Anti-synchronization of Complex-valued Inertial Neural Networks with Distributed Delays
abstract: This paper focuses on studying the problem of fixed-time anti-synchronization(FTAS) and preassigned-time anti-synchronization(PTAS) in complex-valued inertial neural networks with distributed delays. To begin with, by introducing an intermediate variable, we transform the second-order system into the corresponding first-order system. Next, by applying Lyapunov stability theory and the properties of complex numbers, two complex feedback controllers were designed to ensure that the system achieves FTAS and PTAS. Our approach differs from the traditional separation method, as we study the complex-valued system as a unified whole, which reduces computational complexity. In the end, the validity of the obtained results was verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Distributed Time-Varying Nash Equilibrium Algorithm Based on Prediction-Correction Technique with Set Constraints
abstract: In this paper, a class of time-varying noncooperative game problems with set constraints is investigated. A distributed time-varying Nash equilibrium seeking algorithm based on the prediction-correction technique is designed to track the time-varying Nash equilibrium, in which the prediction term based on the Newton’s method is employed to offset the changes of the Nash equilibrium and the correction term enhances the convergence performance. The projection operator is also introduced to settle the set constraints. It is theoretically demonstrated that the proposed algorithm can be tracked within the bounded neighborhood of the time-varying Nash equilibrium under the undirected connectivity graph when appropriate parameters are chosen. Finally numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the algorithm by applying it to solve the formation tracking problem of a multi-USV system.

articleTitle: Optimized Scheduling of Integrated Energy Systems in Dragon Fruit Agricultural Parks
abstract: This paper takes the agricultural electricity load of Guangxi dragon fruit orchard as the background, and constructs a model of light storage and load energy system in agricultural parks. The model comprehensively considers the load characteristics of the speciality agricultural park that are levelable, adjustable and cuttable. A multi-objective optimisation model of the park was established with the objectives of minimising the operating cost of the park and maximising the consumption of new energy, studying the characteristics of supplemental irrigation required for the growth of agricultural orchards, establishing the relevant load regulation model and constraints of the park, solving the model using the Cplex solver in MATLAB, and mapping out the Pareto frontiers by the all-over weighting method, and analysing the influence of the weights on the two objectives, Finally, based on the Pareto frontier diagram, the example is simulated and analysed by choosing appropriate weights, and the results show that it can significantly reduce the cost of power purchase in the park, promote the consumption of renewable energy, and achieve the coordinated operation of the park’s multiple energy sources.

articleTitle: Finite-time Stabilization of Fractional-order Memristive Complex-valued Delay Neural Networks
abstract: This paper focuses on the finite-time(FNT) stabilization for a class of fractional-order memristive complex-valued delay neural networks(FOMCVDNNs). Instead of breaking down the complex-valued system into its real and imaginary components, we have devised a more straightforward approach by introducing a lemma related to the complex-valued sign function. This innovative technique enables us to design a simpler discontinuous controller. In the end, we provide numerical simulations to demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Lagrange Stability of Complex-Valued Memristive Neural Networks with Mixed Time-Varying Delays
abstract: This paper mainly studies the Lagrange exponential stability of complex-valued memristive neural networks (MNNs) with discrete and distributed time delays. Based on differential inclusion and Filippov set-valued mapping theories, some sufficient conditions are given to verify the Lagrange exponential stability and the globally exponentially attractive set is given. Furthermore, when external inputs are not taken into account, Lyapunov stability can be immediately obtained.

articleTitle: Distributed Robust State Estimation of Uncertain Complex Networked Systems
abstract: This paper studies the consensus problem of multi-agent systems with unknown inputs under directed communication topologies. The structure of a specific-time observer is designed which takes a pulsative form at some time instants, and then the distributed attack-free protocol is presented, which only utilizes relative output measurement. To test the validity of the algorithm, the proposed algorithm is compared with existing Kalman filtering algorithm through simulation analysis, thereby drawing a conclusion on the advantages of reducing calculation costs, improving estimation accuracy, and convergence speed.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis of a Fractional-order Memristive Hyperchaotic System
abstract: Combining the ideal magnetic flux-controlled memristor with fractional-order calculus theory, a novel fractional-order memristor model was proposed. Through establishing the mathematical model of the fractional-order memristor, it was verified that the fractional-order memristor satisfies the fundamental characteristics of a memristor, and its memory performance is superior to that of integer-order memristors. Furthermore, the fractional-order memristor was introduced into a four-dimensional chaotic system, resulting in a new fractional-order memristor hyper-chaotic system, which was solved using the Adomian decomposition method. By studying the bifurcation diagrams and Lyapunov exponent spectra with the system’s order, parameters, and initial values as variables, it was observed that varying these factors leads to the manifestation of more complex and diverse dynamical behaviors in the system

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Clustering-Based Approach for Assessing Peak Shifting and Valley Filling Potential in Industrial Electric Loads
abstract: With the advancement of the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, there has been significant development in new energy generation. Due to the intermittency and randomness of new energy generation, it has become more challenging to maintain power balance within the electrical system. Despite significant attention to demand-side management, there remains a lack of effective methods to assess the peak shifting and valley filling potential in a specific region. This paper proposes an industrial electricity load peak shifting and valley filling potential assessment method based on two-stage clustering, aiming to evaluate the potential of industrial users in a particular region. The method relies solely on users’ historical electricity consumption data to evaluate their electricity usage patterns and regularities and subsequently calculates the potential factor for each user. Therefore, this method is universally applicable for assessing any region’s peak shifting and valley filling, the method is applied to assess the peak shifting and valley filling potential in a certain prefecture-level city in China, demonstrating its practical value.

articleTitle: Stochastic Gradients Averaging for Federated Learning Algorithm with Compressed Quantization
abstract: Federated learning presents a promising avenue for training machine learning models across distributed edge networks. Given the inherent data heterogeneity and limited communication bandwidth stemming from the multitude of devices involved, the imperative of curtailing communication costs becomes apparent. While the compressed transmission model stands as a prevalent technique, it solely accommodates uniform data distributions, neglecting the influence of heterogeneous data. This study addresses the challenge by compressing the communication model between devices and the server, grounded in the implementation of stochastic gradient averaging to mitigate errors arising from data heterogeneity. Moreover, the algorithm’s convergence analysis is then provided for non-convex loss functions. The results show that our algorithm has the same convergence order as the stochastic controlled averaging federated learning algorithm. We validate our proposed algorithm using the MNIST and the CIFAR-100 datasets to determine its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Cooperative Power Sharing Can Enhance the Power-flow Balancing in Cyber-Physical Islanded Microgrids
abstract: In islanded AC microgrids, cooperative power-sharing is vital for maintaining stable and secure system operation. Nevertheless, merely focusing on consensus objectives in the secondary control layer is insufficient, as it overlooks potential violations of operational constraints, such as power-flow balance during transient periods. This paper introduces conditions for a droop-controlled, inverter-based islanded microgrid system that ensure compliance with all constraints during transient stability under cooperative control and load fluctuations. As a result, robust and reliable system operation is achieved. We first develop a cyber-physical model that combines the microgrid’s physical oscillator network with its secondary information network. Furthermore, we showcase the significant enhancement of power-flow balance constraint satisfaction in a secondary cooperative control system through the allocation of an active power component. Our findings are illustrated using a numerical case study of a power test system.

articleTitle: Automatic Quality Evaluation for User Generated Contents in Online Q&A Community Based on Word2Vec-CNN
abstract: The online Q&A (question-and-answer) community has emerged as a prominent platform for Internet users to access valuable information, but a notable disparity exists in the quality of answers provided. Hence, understanding and enhancing answer quality evaluation in the context of Chinese Q&A communities assumes paramount significance. First, a system of evaluation metrics for answer quality is constructed. Then, based on this metric system, the collected Zhihu data is annotated and an answer quality automated evaluation model using Word2VecCNN (convolutional neural networks) is developed. Utilize this model to perform both coarse-grained and fine-grained automated evaluation of answer quality in online Q&A communities. Compared to other models, the proposed Word2Vec-CNN-based automatic answer quality evaluation model in this research yielded superior experimental results, particularly in the realms of syntax, semantics, and pragmatics. Furthermore, it closely approximated the manually curated content found in “Zhihu Daily.” It excelled in filtering high-quality answers, significantly enhancing users’ efficiency in acquiring knowledge during their actual browsing experiences within the Q&A community. Consequently, it demonstrates a stronger potential to leverage the pivotal role of Q&A communities in disseminating network knowledge.

articleTitle: Memristor Modeling with Homeostatic Threshold Variation for Simulation and Application
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to emulating biological neural components using memristors. The nanoscale, resistance variability, and non-volatility of the memristor make it a suitable candidate for this task. A homeostasis-type switching mechanism is induced into the memristor modeling, inspired by the homeostatic switching behavior of biological neural components. The proposed model is generalizable and adaptable to various threshold-type memristor models. A SPICE model is proposed, and the memristor model is utilized to implement a neuron circuit that follows the homeostasis-type mechanism. A spiking neural network and its verification platform are designed, where pattern recognition can be achieved. The simulation is carried out in Cadence PSPICE, and a test comparison between scenarios with homeostasis and non-homeostasis is proposed. This work demonstrates the potential of memristors in implementing neuromorphic computing systems.

articleTitle: EEG Channel Selection Based on Neuron Proportion with SNN for Motor Imagery Classification
abstract: The brain computer interface (BCI) technology based on motor imagery has great potential for various control and communication tasks. However, the presence of a large number of EEG channels leads to redundant information, which affects processing speed and classification accuracy. Spiking neural networks (SNN) have the potential to process EEG data by transmitting pulsing activity between synapses and neurons situated in space. Neucube is an SNN architecture inspired by the human brain structure that allows for end-to-end learning, classification, and understanding of spatiotemporal data at low power consumption, saving computing power and reducing operational complexity. By utilizing this model, the temporal and spatial information of EEG signals can be considered to explore the importance and correlation of spatial neurons corresponding to EEG channels during the classification process. Thus, this study aimed to use the Neucube model based on SNN to select the most influential EEG signal channels in the classification process. This improvement mainly focuses on improving classification accuracy and reducing energy consumption to enhance the practical application performance of BCI systems. The proposed method was tested on the BCI Competition IV Dataset 2A. After deleting several unimportant EEG channels, the classification accuracy was improved, and the energy consumption was reduced.

articleTitle: Finite-Time State Estimation for Discrete-Time Complex Networks with Round-Robin Protocol and Uniform Quantization Effects
abstract: In this paper, the finite-time state estimation problem is investigated for a class of discrete-time nonlinear complex networks with Round-Robin protocol and uniform quantization effects. The communication between the nodes of the networks and the state estimator, which is subject to uniform quantization, is carried out through a shared communication medium where only one node is allowed to send data at each transmission moment. To prevent data from collisions, the Round-Robin protocol scheduling is applied to orchestrate the transmission order of nodes in a periodic manner. The main purpose of the addressed problem is to design a state estimator such that, the estimation error is stochastic finite-time bounded. Then, the gains of the state estimator are obtained by solving a set of coupled linear matrix inequalities. Finally, simulation examples are employed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed estimator design scheme.

articleTitle: A Novel Block Focused Omega-K Algorithm for Millimetre-Wave Radar Imaging
abstract: Classical millimetre-wave (mmWave) radar imaging algorithms frequently encounter challenges arising from their substantial computational demands and the complexities inherent in addressing covert imaging effects. In this paper, an original block processing technique is introduced, where the echo data from each antenna is partitioned into two segments along a uniform plane array, simplifying complex matrix operations as observed in traditional approaches such as the back projection algorithm (BPA), the range-Doppler algorithm (RDA), and the omega-k ($\omega k$) algorithm. Additionally, a novel focusing step is introduced to increase the strength of the target signal at low signal-to-noise ratios, which entails partitioning the two-dimensional Fourier-transformed domain echo data into blocks based on the distance dimension. These improvements are integrated into the conventional $\omega k$ algorithm, yielding the proposed ”Block Focused Omega-k” (BF-$\omega k$) algorithm. Finally, a real experimental platform is established employing the official Ti IWR1642 experimental board. The effectiveness of the introduced algorithm is demonstrated through both simulation experiments and physical experiments. Extensive trials have been conducted encompassing imaging under varying signal-to-noise ratios and compression ratios, and the imaging of exposed and concealed objects across both single-target and multi-target scenarios.

articleTitle: Stacking Integration Strategy-Based Learning Method for Prediction of Performance in Exams
abstract: Academic performance serves as a direct indicator of learning effectiveness. In the paper, a stacking learning method is proposed to predict students’ performance in exam. Firstly, an in-depth correlation analysis is conducted to examine various factors, including students’ school situation and exam scores in other subjects, which have an impact on the exam scores in a specific subject. It is found that a strong correlation exists between exam scores in different subjects, and factors such as students’ lunch level and parents’ education level significantly impact these scores. Secondly, the stacking integration strategy employs Random Forest (RF) as the base learner, while the random gradient model is selected as the meta learner to construct a predictive model for learning achievement. Finally, a comparative experiment is conducted using multiple models, including Decision Trees (DT) and support vector machines (SVM), to predict students’ exam scores. The results show that the learning achievement prediction model based on the stacking integration strategy outperforms all other tested models, exhibiting an accuracy improvement ranging from 6% to 17%. Moreover, its performance in statistical evaluation indicators and error evaluation indicators are well. The proposed learning method is more efficient to predict students’ performance in exams.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Semi-Supervised Method for Remote Sensing Scene Classification Based on Class-Related Complexity Index
abstract: Remote sensing image scene classification has been extensively studied, and a significant proportion of solutions for this task are based on deep learning techniques nowadays. Although powerful, deep learning models usually require large amounts of labeled data for training, and labels for remote sensing images are usually hard to obtain and expensive. To alleviate this problem, semi-supervised learning has been proposed to train classifiers using both labeled and unlabeled samples. In this paper, we propose an improved method for labeled sample products based on consistency regularization. This method performs sample selection through a dynamic threshold mechanism based on a class-related complexity index. In the field of remote sensing image scene classification, this method can be used in the framework of semi-supervised learning to perform better sample set expansion according to the semantic complexity of different classes.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Neutral Stochastic Pantograph System with Time-dependent Switching and its Applications in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the stability of a highly non-linear neutral stochastic pantograph system with time-dependent switching (NSPSTS) and its applications in neural networks. Firstly, the concept of switching density is introduced to describe the switching frequency of the nonlinear switching system. Subsequently, under the novel switching mechanism, by utilizing the Lyapunov function technique and stochastic theory, the existence and uniqueness of the solution of NSPSTS are discussed, and one criterion on pth moment $\psi-$stability is derived. Moreover, the presented findings are applied to neural networks (NNs). At last, an example is presented to demonstrate the validity of the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: A Generalized Continuous-Time Algorithm for Nonsmooth Distributed Convex Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a generalized continuous-time algorithm with a novel auxiliary function to solve a nonsmooth distributed constraint optimization over undirected network. By virtue of the property of auxiliary function, the state solution of continuous-time algorithm is proven to enter the sets of equality and inequality constraints in finite time and stay there forever. Moreover, we demonstrate that the proposed algorithm reaches consensus and finally converges to the optimal solution under several mild assumptions. In contrast to the existing algorithms, the proposed algorithm has the simple structure with fewer state variables. Finally, the simulation results and an application in power system are given to show the efficacy and practicability of the presented algorithm.

articleTitle: Meta-PolyArc:A Face Recognition Algorithm for Truck Drivers at Unmanned Gates Aiming at Few-shot Problem
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the face recognition problem of transport drivers in unmanned gate scenarios. In this scenario, due to the high cost of data collection, the on-site data comes from video frame interception, the repetition rate under the same ID is high, and the data sets used for fine-tuning all have the Few-shot problem. Through experiments, we found that the face recognition model pre-trained on public datasets and simple fine-tuning are difficult to meet the actual needs of the field. In addition, the inference speed of the network is limited by the depth of the network, which is not enough to meet the actual needs. Inspired by some scholars’ solutions to the Few-shot problem, we propose a solution: adopt the Meta-Learning training method, and apply several classifier generation methods to solve the Few-shot problem to the recognition model. In order to further speed up network reasoning, we apply the latest CNN architecture model: FasterNet to the face recognition network. In order to further improve its accuracy, the ArcPoly loss function is proposed by combining the longitudinally designed PolyLoss and the ArcFace loss function based on metric learning. We have achieved an accuracy rate of 95.69% and 61FPS in the unmanned gate transport driver recognition scenario, which meets the actual application requirements.

articleTitle: Improved EEG Decoding Method Based on Spiking Neural Network for SSVEPs’ Classification
abstract: This paper presents an electroencephalogram (EEG) signals decoding method based on an event-driven spiking neural network (SNN) model design for steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP) tasks’ classification and recognition. Adopting the approach of data-driven ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) of little additional input parameters, the original signals is enhanced to obtain relatively accurate EEG data with valid SSVEP characteristics, which strengthen the signal-to-noise (SNR) at the stimulation frequency. A canonical correlation analysis (CCA) method is considered to be applied to extract frequency characteristics from the multi-lead EEG data, declining the amount of data and training overhead. The training samples with correlation coefficient vectors are sampled into sparse spike sequences through the level crossing (LC) coding and input directly to a resembled excitation–inhibition (E–I) balanced SNN model in the way of event-driven processing. With the sparse data representation, the SNN model adopts the approaches of sparse training and neuromorphic computing to perform pattern recognition for the SNN-compatible spikes. On the Wearable SSVEP-BCI dataset and BETA database provided by Tsinghua University for 12-target and 40-target EEG classification, this SNN method can achieve 96.95% and 89.72% classification accuracy, with 99.66 bits/min and 130.26 bits/min information transfer rate (ITR), respectively.

articleTitle: 3DNesT: A Hierarchical Local Self-Attention Model for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease. Brain atrophy is one of the most common hallmarks of AD, which can be accessed by structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI). Recent advances in deep learning models based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) have led to excellent results in classifying AD from normal controls (NC). Inspired by the concept of brain connections, we proposed a 3D Nested Hierarchical Transformer (3DNesT) model featuring a hierarchical local self-attention mechanism for diagnosing AD and provided the interpretation of the model. We calculated the attention of regions within each single block and merged the blocks hierarchically to integrate the information throughout the brain for diagnosis. Using sMRI from 1159 NC and 833 AD from three multisite datasets, the proposed model achieves 90.06±2.26% accuracy in 10-fold cross-validation and 82.70%, 90.08%, and 91.60% in inter-site cross-validation. Our model has more trainable parameters and achieves better accuracy with less memory cost than the traditional CNN model. The model puts more attention in the medial temporal lobe when identifying NC, while the attention is spread out when predicting AD. Furthermore, the predicted values were significantly correlated with cognitive scores and key neurobiological indicators in AD, demonstrating the clinical validity of the 3DNesT model.

articleTitle: Vehicle Intelligent Application System Based on Improved YOLOv5 and DeepSORT
abstract: Nowadays, the coverage of the expressway is constantly expanding, and the traffic volume on each highway is also rapidly expanding. This research suggests a vehicle analysis system based on YOLOv5+DeepSORT to overcome the poor real-time performance of conventional traffic statistics and low accuracy in detection for original algorithms. In this paper, we propose a method named YOLOv5-Car based on YOLOv5 model, which mAP is 1.6% higher than that of the YOLOv5 model. The YOLOv5 model is improved in 2 ways: (1) When the Coordinate Attention (CoordAtt) module is added to the YOLOv5 backbone network, channel attention is divided into two 1-dimensional feature coding processes and aggregated along two spatial directions, respectively. This method can enhance the position and depiction of interesting objects in the input feature map. (2) Replace the Non Maximum Suppression (NMS) based technique with the more accurate and completely parallelizable Confidence Propagation Cluster (CP-Cluster). The outcomes of the experiments show that the strategy suggested in this study can improve the precision of the vehicle analysis system.

articleTitle: Chaotic Oscillation Systems with Disturbance Based on DNA Strand Displacement and Its Active Control
abstract: The emergence of DNA strand displacement (DSD) technology has facilitated the development of chaotic synchronization. The active control of the three-variable chaotic oscillation system is designed with DSD technology in this paper. Firstly, DNA strands are designed according to base complementary pairing. The biochemical modules of double, catalysis, subtraction, displacement, and degradation are constructed based on the designed DNA strands. Secondly, the biochemical modules are used to construct the drive system reaction networks and the response system reaction networks with unknown disturbances. Thirdly, an error-compensation active controller is designed based on the DSD technique, which is added to the chaotic oscillation system to achieve synchronous control of the chaotic systems. The biochemical modules and the chaotic systems are carried out and tested by making use of the MATLAB and Visual DSD software. The simulation results show that it is feasible for us to use DSD technology to realize the active control of chaotic oscillation system. This paper may be used to the more complex controlled objective of multivariable chaotic system based on DSD.

articleTitle: Lightweight YOLOv5 Gesture Recognition Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a lightweight LS-YOLOv5 network to address the drawbacks of existing gesture recognition algorithm models, such as complexity and large memory usage. The aim is to achieve real-time recognition on embedded devices. Firstly, a lightweight ShuffleNetV2 network and CBRM module are added to the YOLOv5 to achieve model lightweight. The ECA attention mechanism is also incorporated to boost feature representation and enhance detection precision. Finally, the SIoU loss function is used to enable more precise target localization and prediction. By conducting experiments on a gesture dataset with 10 categories, the performance and accuracy of a gesture recognition algorithm were tested. The results showed that the LS-YOLOv5 network model reduced parameter and floating-point computation by 45.7% and 48.7%, respectively, while achieving a certain degree of accuracy improvement. The model can be deployed on edge terminals.

articleTitle: RP-MSTC*: Multi-Agent Coverage Path Planning Algorithm Emphasizing Local Area Updates
abstract: Compared to traditional area coverage algorithms, this paper proposes a re-plannable multi-agent coverage path planning algorithm to address issues such as low coverage rate of multiple agents in large-scale scenarios like warehouses and inability to cope with local environmental changes. Initially, the MSTC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> algorithm is utilized to create the coverage path based on the available map information. To address scenarios like idle areas for material placement, the method introduces local area detection and path re-planning to enhance the coverage rate. This paper verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of the algorithm under different maps through simulation experiments. Compared with the coverage situation of other coverage path planning algorithms in environments with local area updates, the algorithm proposed in this paper has a higher coverage rate in this scenario.

articleTitle: Distributed Nash Equilibrium Seeking Under Dynamic Event-Triggered Mechanism Without Velocity Measurement
abstract: In this paper, the noncooperative game with second-order nonlinear systems is studied. To seek the Nash equilibrium (NE) for each player with second-order nonlinear dynamics, a distributed NE seeking algorithm is proposed. Therein, considering the difficulty of obtaining velocity information in the real physical system, this paper adopts the filter-based method that utilizes the single-layer velocity observation system to quickly obtain the accurate speed estimation information of the player, so as to reduce the system cost. At the same time, to make reasonable use of communication resources and reduce communication overhead among players, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism driven by inner variable is provided. It avoids Zeno-behavior while achieving NE seeking. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed algorithm are demonstrated through an instance of multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAVs) systems.

articleTitle: Finite-Level Quantized Iterative Learning Control for a Class of Fuzzy Cellular Neural Networks Based on Encoding-Decoding Mechanism
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of finite-level uniform quantized iterative learning control for a class of fuzzy cellular neural networks employing an encoding-decoding scheme. The proposed approach involves encoding the fuzzy cellular neural network system state signal into uncomplicated data, which is subsequently broadcasted to the controller. The encoded data is then utilized to update the system input, while the decoder estimates the sender’s state. To achieve consensus tracking convergence and alleviate communication burden, one will introduce a uniform quantizer to quantity the information and establish an iterative learning protocol using the estimated tracking error. The effectiveness of the proposed protocol is demonstrated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Stock Market’s Price Movement Prediction with Multi-branch LSTM and Technical Analysis
abstract: The relationship between technical indicators and stock market trading decision-making is investigated in this paper. Inspired by the technical analysis method, the technical indicators that are used as auxiliary information in many studies are the only source of information given to the prediction model proposed in this paper. The integrated learning method is used to combine the technical indicators and prediction models into a multi-branch Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. Prediction accuracy is obtained when various technical indicators are used as the input of the prediction model. The experiment results show that a combination of neural networks and technical indicators can achieve better prediction accuracy in the task of stock price movements. This multi-branch LSTM model has achieved an accuracy of 70% when predicting the stock price movement of the Shanghai Composite Index.

articleTitle: Extreme Sparsity in Hodgkin-Huxley Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: Spiking neural networks present a new generation of artificial neural networks utilizing binary data representation for large energy, memory, and latency savings due to widespread sparsity. At the same time, they are at the focal point for neuroscientific communities, enabling biologically plausible simulations of systems with a learning capacity. In this work, we present spiking neural networks based on an implementation of a biologically highly plausible neuron model, the Hodgkin-Huxley model. The networks are trained via backpropagation through time using surrogate gradients. They show competitive performances on various neuromorphic datasets while displaying a spiking activity lower by up to two orders of magnitude compared to similar spiking neural networks based on the conventional leaky integrate-and-fire neuron model. Additionally, this work paves the way toward higher biological plausibility in high-performance computational neuroscience by enabling in-depth looks at the underlying dynamics of Hodgkin-Huxley neurons as part of larger operating networks.

articleTitle: A CNN-Transformer-Based Multimodal Model for Cardiac Abnormal Signal Detection
abstract: Cardiovascular disease detection plays a crucial role in medical diagnosis, and deep learning models have shown promise in analyzing physiological signals such as electrocar-diogram (ECG) and phonocardiogram (PCG). In this study, we propose a multimodal model that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) and Transformer. Our model harnesses the information embedded in both ECG and PCG signals, thereby enhancing the detection capability of cardiac abnormalities. A channel attention mechanism is introduced in the CNN module, while the Transformer module captures long-range dependencies. Experimental results on a real world dataset show the effectiveness of our approach. Our model is also designed to accommodate other modalities, such as EEG and tabular data. The proposed model offers a flexible and effective solution for multimodal cardiac abnormality detection.

articleTitle: Efficient Memristive Binary Neural Networks With Spatial Separable Convolutions
abstract: The binary neural network (BNN) is an attractive model for edge computing, and memristor-based neuromorphic computing platform provides competitive end-side deployment scheme. However, current BNNs still have massive convolutional kernel parameters, which remain an obstacle to their deployment on end-side computing platform. In this paper, an efficient BNN called BSSC-Net is proposed, which applies binary spatial separable convolution (BSSC) to reduce the parameters of the binary convolutional kernels. Furthermore, a BNN training framework called KDSNG-BNN is designed to improve the performance of BSSC-Net, which consists of a full-precision model, a BSSCNet, and a discriminator with spectral normalization layers. In this framework, our proposed BSSC-Net can improve the ability to learn feature distributions by simultaneously performing distillation and adversarial training. Experimental results show that the proposed BSSC-Net and BSSC-Net-I based on ResNet-18 trained in KDSNG-BNN can achieve 93.36% and 93.32% accuracy on CIFAR-10, outperforming ReActNet by 0.81% and 0.77%, respectively, and the convolutional kernel parameters of the BSSC-Net and BSSC-Net-I are only 81% and 76.3% of ReActNet. Meanwhile, current memristor technology is more suitable for supporting the computation of low-bit parameters, while BNN quantizes weights and activations to 1 bit, which is ideal for deployment on memristors. Therefore, this paper presents a memristive implementation scheme by exploiting the advantages of memristors and BSSC-Net, intending to realize and promote end-side intelligent applications.

articleTitle: Confidence Estimation Based on the Explanations of Model’s Predictions
abstract: Estimating the confidence of a machine learning (ML) model plays an important role in minimizing undesirable outcomes and safety risks when using ML models in the real world, especially in high-stake application scenarios. However, the majority of existing confidence estimation methods do not work well without incorporating internal information from the model, such as the gradients, internal representations or checkpoints of its training process, which might compromise the security of the model. To alleviate such limitations, we intend to design a reliable confidence estimation method that requires as little internal model information as possible, yet precisely detecting uncertain samples for the model. In this work, we propose a confidence estimation approach that learns the confidence criterion (that is, the true class probability, TCP) based on the explanations of model’s predictions. The proposed approach utilizes the knowledge learned in the model with the leverage of the explanations for model’s prediction rather than directly extracting internal information of the model, so that it can be adopted in a wide range of applications. Several experiments, including experiments on different datasets, different models and non-IID (independent and identically distributed) test datasets, are conducted to examine the effectiveness of our confidence estimation method. The experimental results show that our proposed approach provides a reliable confidence estimation and generally performs better than the compared methods, especially in the capability of recognizing when a ML model makes errors.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Domain of Attraction on Controlled Complex Networks with Unbounded Time-varying Delay
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of the domain of attraction (DOA) estimation for complex networks with unbounded delay. Firstly, from the perspective of $\gamma -$stability, a time-varying differential inequality with unbounded time-varying is established, and various stabilities including polynomial stability and logarithmic stability are discussed. By removing restrictive monotonicity conditions, a novel inequality is developed. Subsequently, based on the proposed differential inequalities and the Lyapunov function approach, the local synchronization of complex network system with unbounded delay has been analyzed and some criteria for the DOA estimation are derived. Finally, two numerical examples are presented to verify the feasibility of theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Improve Adversarial Robustness via Probabilistic Distributions Decoupled Network While Guaranteeing Clean Performance
abstract: The deep neural network (DNN) can be fooled by introducing a small perturbation to the example. Adversarial training (AT) is proven to be one of the most effective methods to improve robustness. Although the latest works to improve AT can ensure the adversarial robustness of PGD, the exploration of the performance under more disturbances is lacking, which may lead to our misunderstanding of model generalization. Moreover, they sacrifice DNN’s performance of classifying clean examples, which is called clean performance. Research shows that overfitting will be caused by the cross-mixing of distributions between natural and adversarial examples. We discover that the primary cause of cross-mixing is using the same batch-normalization (BN) layer to normalize the natural and adversarial examples because their means and variances are substantially different. We propose a new defense method which is called probabilistic distributions alignment adversarial training (PDAT). It utilizes the model with a multi-BN structure, which contains natural BN (NBN) and adversarial BN (ABN) to normalize the natural and adversarial examples separately and calculate their corresponding probabilistic distributions. It mutually trains the model through the alignment of probabilistic distributions between NBN and ABN. The natural training (NT) process of NBN is utilized to guide the training process of ABN which is much more difficult. To ensure that the model learns the correct knowledge during the alignment process, we use dynamic weights and soft-decision schemes in the loss function. This alleviates the cross-mixing problem. We conduct experiments on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 and verify that PDAT improves robustness across a wide range of attacks while maximally maintaining clean performance. This proves that PDAT generalizes better.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Synchronization of Impulsive Multi-layer Networks with Time-Varying Parameters Uncertainty
abstract: This article is devoted to fixed-time synchronization (FXTS) for a type of impulsive multi-layer networks (IMNs) having time-varying parameters uncertainty. Firstly, impulsive effects and parameter uncertainty are introduced into the modelling of multi-layer complex networks. Besides, by developing a time-varying Lyapunov function, a concise criterion composed of matrix inequalities is established to ensure the FXTS of the considered IMNs by exploiting Schur complement theory, which makes it less conservative than existing relevant results. A numerical simulation is utilized at last to certify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Quantizated Federated Learning Algorithm with Server Momentum Aggregation*
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) represents a rapidly advancing technique that empowers multiple workers to collaboratively train a global model using a distributed dataset. However, FL frequently grapples with the challenge of unstable and sluggish convergence attributed to the heterogeneous attributes of participating clients. By incorporating an additional momentum step, showcasing its efficacy across both centralized and FL scenarios The need to mitigate the substantial communication costs arising from server-client synchronization while propelling model convergence serves as the driving force behind the proposition of the quantizated federated learning algorithm with server momentum aggregation (SMFedCOM) algorithm. This algorithm involves refining the process of updating global model parameters. The integration of Nesterov momentum terms on the server side not only bolsters the stability of server-side aggregation but also employs parameter quantization to curtail communication overhead. A detailed convergence analysis of the SMFedCOM algorithm is given, substantiating that its convergence rate aligns with the non-convex nature of the objective function. Specifically, this rate is characterized as $\mathcal{O}\left(1 / \sqrt{N T K}+1 / T^{2}\right)$, with N denoting the count of participating clients, K representing the number of local training iterations, and T indicating the total number of iterations. The algorithm is compared with existing algorithms via numerical simulations based on benchmark datasets. Empirical results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively accelerate the convergence of the model.

articleTitle: MI-MAMI: Multisensory Integration Model Inspired by the Macro and Micro Mechanisms of the Human Brain
abstract: The interaction between information from different senses is crucial for multisensory integration. Without the interaction, traditional deep learning methods exhibit inferior performance in the integration. On the contrary, the human brain has an inherently remarkable ability in this area, which stems from the macro and micro brain networks. Based on this superiority, we propose a brain-inspired model called MI-MAMI (Multisensory Integration model inspired by the MAcro and MIcro mechanisms). Aligning with the macro brain network that consists of unisensory pathways and integration regions, a similar framework of the MI-MAMI is established. The MI-MAMI incorporates unisensory processing streams and an integration block, enabling the comprehensive integration of multisensory information. In addition, inspired by the diverse neurons and the synaptic connections found in integration regions, we innovatively design weight constraints to regulate information transmission among neurons. Leveraging these mechanisms at both the macro and micro levels, our model is biologically plausible and enables more effective interaction and integration. To validate the performance of the MI-MAMI model, we conducted a case study focusing on multisensory emotion recognition. The results show that our model surpasses state-of-the-art brain-inspired baselines on RAVDESS and eNTERFACE’05 datasets, showcasing the potential of brain-inspired methods for advancing multisensory integration.

articleTitle: Privacy Preserving Discretized Spiking Neural Network with TFHE
abstract: Artificial intelligence not only offers significant convenience but also raises privacy and security concerns, which pose challenges for Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs). Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a crucial privacy-preserving computation technology, and the discrete nature of SNNs naturally aligns with FHE’s requirements. In this paper, we construct a framework to evaluate the homomorphic computation of SNN named FHE-DiSNN that enables SNN to achieve good prediction performance on encrypted data. First, benefitting from the discrete nature of spike signals, our proposed model avoids the errors introduced by discretizing activation functions. Second, by applying bootstrapping, we design new privacy-preserving functions FHE-Fire and FHE-Reset, through which noise can be refreshed, allowing us to evaluate SNN for an arbitrary number of operations. Furthermore, we improve the computational efficiency of FHE-DiSNN while maintaining a high level of accuracy. Finally, we evaluate our model on the MNIST dataset. The experiments show that FHE-DiSNN with 30 neurons in the hidden layer achieves a minimum prediction accuracy of 94.4%. Under optimal parameters, it achieves a 95.1% accuracy, with only a 0.6% decrease compared to the original SNN (95.7%). These results demonstrate the superiority of SNN over second-generation neural networks for homomorphic evaluation.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Robust Optimization for Integrated Energy Systems with Power-to-Gas and Demand Response
abstract: Integrated energy systems are an important means of energy management. The coordinated operation of various energy devices facilitates the efficient operation of the system on the supply side, while demand response enables peak shaving and valley filling of loads on the demand side. Meanwhile, the system’s operation is subject to various uncertainties. Therefore, this paper proposes a two-stage robust optimization scheduling strategy for integrated energy systems that considers power-to-gas (P2G) and demand response. The model of the integrated energy system incorporates the synergistic utilization of P2G devices and gas storage devices, as well as the engagement of flexible loads in demand response. The two-stage robust optimization method is employed to handle uncertainties associated with wind power and basic load during system scheduling, and the Column-and-Constraint Generation (C& CG) algorithm and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) condition are utilized for solving the optimization problem. Experimental results demonstrate that the integration of P2G devices and demand response enhances the system’s economic performance, while the robust optimization enables the system to withstand fluctuations caused by uncertainties.

articleTitle: Memristive Binary Firefly Algorithm for White Lung Images Segmentation
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of designing and employing swarm intelligence algorithms using memristors. As a representative swarm intelligence algorithm, the firefly algorithm is binarized and implemented through a memristor crossbar array to facilitate image threshold segmentation. Firstly, a memristor crossbar array with an external control circuit is meticulously designed, presenting both elevated device density and the potential for parallel computing. Secondly, the binary firefly algorithm is enacted through this memristor crossbar array. Finally, the method is put to practical use by applying it to the segmentation of medical images, the threshold can be directly calculated from the current and charge within the crossbar array. Notably, the error rate of our crossbar-based binary firefly algorithm implementation is significantly low compared to the brute-force method.

articleTitle: Research on the Calculation Method for Carbon Emission Responsibility in Power System Based on Carbon Flow Theory and Fairness Principle
abstract: In order to accurately calculate the carbon liability of load nodes in new-type power system and promote the continuous development of low-carbon power, in this paper, the carbon potential and carbon liability of load nodes was firstly estimated based on carbon emission stream theory. Secondly, the initial carbon potential of the load nodes was modified through using the Comprehensive Load (CL) method, which comprehensively considers the electricity consumption characteristics of load nodes.
