Next, the fairness interval of carbon reduction responsibility reflecting long-term electricity consumption characteristics of the region was established by considering long-term electricity demand variation of the load nodes. Finally, the satisfaction degree of each load node with the calculation results of carbon emission responsibility was accurately evaluated accordingly, which pointed out the direction for low-carbon transition strategy generation and demand-side response capacity construction of the power system. The application results in the 14-node system demonstrated that, compared with calculated carbon emission responsibility results based on initial carbon potential, the estimated results of the load nodes considering customer’s electricity consumption characteristics are both reasonable and accurate, which provide the data support for clean and lowcarbon development of the power industry, with broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Distributed Attack-Resilient Nash Equilibrium Seeking for Networked Games: An Event-Triggered Extended State Observer Approach
abstract: For the non-cooperative game in networked systems with individuals having the second-order dynamics, a new resilient distributed Nash Equilibrium (NE) seeking algorithm with only strategies on event-triggered time instants is proposed when considering attacks target the actuators and sensors. Malicious attacks are assumed to inject some unknown false data into each agent’s control inputs and also manipulate the exchanging information between agents. In order to alleviate the negative impacts of attacks on the agents’ strategies, an event-triggered extended state observer (ET-ESO) with dynamic event-triggered condition is proposed. The designed ET-ESO aims to approximate both agents’ strategies and attack signals by regarding the attack signals as extended states. The estimation can be made with arbitrary accuracy directly related to the ESO parameter. The Zeno behavior is also proved to be excluded related to the ETESO. The attack-resilient NE seeking algorithm with distributed manner is then proposed based on such ET-ESO, and agents’ strategies would converge to an arbitrary small bound around the NE despite unknown injected cyber attack signals. Lastly, a numerical example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained results.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Event-Triggered Mean-Square Consensus Control for Discrete-Time Stochastic Multi-Agent System With System Uncertainties
abstract: In this paper, the mean-square consistency control problem of a class of discrete time-varying multi-agent systems with system parameter uncertainty and a dynamic event-triggering mechanism is studied. Using a dynamic event-based mechanism, each agent only updates the control input signal when it violates the pre-set triggering conditions. A mean-square consistent performance index is used to reflect the transient consistent behavior of the deviation degree between each agent and the mean of the average state of the whole system. For a fixed network communication topology, the purpose is to design a time-varying feedback controller so that each agent’s mean square consistency index in each time step can satisfy the given upper bound constraint under the disturbance of external disturbances in the closed-loop network multi-agent system. Then, the feedback gain is obtained by solving the solution of recursive linear matrix inequality. Finally, a simulation example is given to illustrate the authenticity and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Container Truck Detection and Re-identification in Terminal Scenarios
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the use of QR code to identify the roof number in the loading and unloading area of the terminal is difficult to maintain, and the recognition accuracy is gradually reduced, and the identification of truck collection is more quickly and accurately, this paper analyzes the characteristics of truck re-identification based on the general vehicle re-identification task, takes the CenterNet network as the baseline model, and optimizes the model from three aspects: backbone network, attention mechanism and feature fusion for the detection difficulties of truck features. Most importantly, based on the truck feature detection results, this paper proposes a vehicle re-recognition algorithm based on global and local feature fusion, which optimizes the model by joint multi-branch loss, and proposes a reordering algorithm based on the roof number recognition results to improve the re-recognition accuracy of the model. In this paper, the vehicle detection network, text recognition network and vehicle re-identification network are combined to construct a truck re-identification model and apply it to the port truck recognition task. The set truck re-identification dataset in this paper includes 239 images, the gallery set includes 1161 truck set images, and the truck re-identification model achieves 91.4% rank-1 accuracy and 96.2% rank-5 accuracy on this dataset, and the inference time of a single image is about 1.6s, which meets the needs of engineering applications.

articleTitle: Secure Consensus of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems Under Limited Communication Bandwidth and DoS Attacks
abstract: In this paper, secure consensus of uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems is studied under the constrains of limited bandwidth and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. A double-loop controller is proposed, where a sampling-based encoding-decoding scheme is considered in outer-loop controller to handle the limited bandwidth of communication channel, and sliding model control approach and neuro-adaptive law are designed in inner-loop to deal with the uncertainty of nonlinear systems. Secure consensus is achieved under the control strategy when DoS attacks are subject to mild constrains in the form of frequency and duration. Simulations are given to verify the effectiveness of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Distributed Power Distribution Management in AC Microgrids Using Game Theoretical Approach
abstract: Recent advancements in the modern grid and energy sector have pivoted the focus towards the optimal power allocation of large-scale distributed generator (DG) units, especially when user-generated power integrates with microgrids (MGs). This study employs the Cournot oligopoly game to ascertain the Nash equilibrium between the power generation company and the power generation user when the MG operates in an island mode. Through this Nash equilibrium, we determine the ideal proportion of power production between the company and the user. To maximize the benefits and maintain MG stability, we introduce a distributed control approach rooted in consensus theory. This methodology prompts each DG to adjust its power output in line with the collective consumption load. By leveraging the Nash equilibrium-derived optimal power generation ratio, we effectively eradicate the steady-state frequency deviation across all DG units within the MG, consequently upholding power quality standards for users. Simulation outcomes affirm the efficacy of our proposed control strategy in meeting the outlined research objectives.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Stability Analysis and Stabilization of Discrete-Time Stochastic Time-Varying Systems with Time Delay via the Interval-Matrix Method
abstract: This paper investigates the finite-time stochastic stability (FTSS) and stabilization of discrete-time stochastic time-varying systems (DSTSs) with time delay. Within the framework of differential inclusions, the DSTSs are first transformed into systems with interval parameters. Utilizing novel Lyapunov-Krasovskii function (LKF) and linear matrix inequalities(LMIs), sufficient conditions for FTSS of the systems are proposed. Additionally, by applying state feedback, suitable controllers are designed to achieve finite-time stabilization of the systems. However, this approach unavoidably introduces conservatism, leading to increased control costs and energy consumption. Therefore, we propose a new piecewise control method to reduce control costs. Finally, simulation examples are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed approach.
